fixture.limitation: Provisional until the first real save. This world is synthetic: it exercises the shape of a save (terrain, caves, overhangs, structures and mixed materials) but was not produced by gameplay, by docs/specs/worldgen-design.md, or by the save path on the reference machine. Its byte sizes, material histograms and distributions are illustrative only and must not be quoted as gate results (M1-35, M1-37) until a real save is captured and this fixture is re-frozen.

rows.pre_registered: 40% of 8,188 MiB = 3,275 MiB; hard fail at 60% = 4,913 MiB
rows.note: Projected from the measured p95 total per chunk; the max chunk (3.80 MiB) would project to 2.98 GiB. The target row is 3.20 GiB (+219.26 MiB), the hard-fail row is 4.80 GiB (+1.81 GiB). The gate uses p95 by pre-registration, not the mean, and does not apply the 1.5× factor a second time.

rows.pre_registered: Per profile and edge, table §2: N64 = 6,432, N128 = 804
rows.measured: N64 = 6,440 at 64³; N128 = 805 at 128³ equal volume
rows.note: The gate asserts the frozen model's equal-volume identity, N64 = 8 × N128. The table's own N64/N128 are a prediction: measured 6,440 / 805 against 6,432 / 804 (deltas +8 / +1). Those deltas are the table's nearest-integer rounding and are reported, not folded back into the model. N64 feeds the memory projection.

The node count is the banded internal-node arena (`dag_node_bytes / 8`), so it is a hard per-chunk cap, not a p95. The other edge's budget is pre-registered but not measured by this build; M1-40 supplies the 128³ projection before M1-42.

One 16 B cell per block, fixed by the compiled chunk edge. The 128³ value is the frozen pre-registration target and is not built in M1. This is an invariant of the memory model, which charges exactly this volume; a resident `LightState` also allocates propagation scratch, which this gate does not measure.

One 12 B SH4 RGB probe per block at the near LOD. The update row measures the latency; this row checks the fixed grid and the byte volume the model charges, which is an invariant rather than a resident allocation. The 128³ value is pre-registered, not built in M1.

rows.measured: p95 2115 KiB (max 2115 KiB); production AO / M3-00 packed 8 B vertex + u16 index (44 B/quad) + records
rows.source: gate memory (M1-35); production AO mesher; M1-31 reference
rows.note: The production AO mesh is measured through `mesh_block` and charged as M3-00 packed 8 B vertex + u16 index (44 B/quad) plus 16 B per non-empty block meshlet record and the per-chunk u16 record table. The M1-31 no-AO reference is 2519 KiB p95, informational only and not in the total. The predicted lower bound is 150 KiB; a lower estimate is not a failure. The gate uses p95 and reports max separately.

rows.pre_registered: p95 ≤ 8 ms (consolidate + upload + fence + flip + dirty light)
rows.note: Fixed = upload + fence + flip; dirty = COW + light. The fence and upload are the CPU side of the M4 protocol; the headless gate has no GPU device time, so this is a lower bound on a real device path, not a claim about GPU completion.

rows.measured: p95 745.095 µs (p50 603.586 µs, max 3.29 ms); 1,000 edited chunks
rows.note: Update = select + rebake + upload. Only probes whose rays reach the dirty voxel are rebaked; the upload is the CPU staging copy and excludes the device transfer and the M4 fence/flip.

rows.pre_registered: ≤ 15% traversed-but-invisible at chunk boundaries @ max view
rows.note: Reference frustum traversal at block resolution against the M1-33 occlusion oracle, on the frozen save. The reference fill is conservative: a partly filled block is passable, so on this terrain save almost everything is reachable and a 0.00% result is non-discriminating. It is the baseline the M5 production culler must beat; a missed reference-visible block would be a correctness failure, not granularity.

This is an invariant on the frozen budget, not a second measurement. The factor survives hardware changes because the fraction (40%/60%) does; applying it twice would make the gate stricter than the pre-registration.

rows.pre_registered: Real populated save; median, p95, max per chunk
rows.note: Provisional until the first real save. This world is synthetic: it exercises the shape of a save (terrain, caves, overhangs, structures and mixed materials) but was not produced by gameplay, by docs/specs/worldgen-design.md, or by the save path on the reference machine. Its byte sizes, material histograms and distributions are illustrative only and must not be quoted as gate results (M1-35, M1-37) until a real save is captured and this fixture is re-frozen. The distributions are measured (p50/p95/max per chunk), but the dataset is not admissible as the M1 gate result until a real populated save replaces it.

rows.pre_registered: See §4; pre-registered; no renegotiation inside M1
rows.measured: not triggered by the measured rows
rows.note: No measured row triggers a §4 fallback. The real-save dataset remains outstanding before the gate can be green. If a later memory row fails at 128³, rule 3 applies: mesh compression, then near radius, then vertical shell; never shrink the far clip below 8 km.

fallback.action: No measured row triggers a §4 fallback. The real-save dataset remains outstanding before the gate can be green. If a later memory row fails at 128³, rule 3 applies: mesh compression, then near radius, then vertical shell; never shrink the far clip below 8 km.

notes: The twelve rows are the frozen table in docs/specs/pre-registration.md §3. Every verdict is computed from a measured value, a checked invariant, or is not_measured; no row is typed PASS. A row the M1-35…M1-38 harnesses do not measure is NOT MEASURED, not green.

The memory projection is the measured p95 per-chunk total multiplied by the loaded chunk count at the edge this build uses. It applies the frozen 60% hard-fail line (4,913 MiB); the 1.5× safety factor is already inside that line, so it is not applied twice.
The headless gate does not open a wgpu adapter. GPU identity is quoted from docs/specs/reference-machine.md and is not re-probed; the host CPU, OS and architecture are read from the running process.

The fixture is provisional until the first real save. Its distributions are a rehearsal for the gate and must not be quoted as the M1 result; the dataset row stays not measured until a real save replaces it.

Culling granularity is measured by the M1-34 reference over 100 poses on the frozen save. The reference traversal is frustum-only, so its ratio is the baseline the M5 production occlusion culler must beat.
The fallback is computed from the measured rows with the pre-registration §4 order. It is a preview, not a renegotiation of any threshold.
